articles.title: Every Drop Counts
articles.note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Water covers most of the Earth, but only a very small part of it is fresh water that people can drink. In dry seasons, some places do not have enough.
Saving water at home is easy. Turn off the tap while you brush your teeth. Take shorter showers. Fix leaks quickly, because a dripping tap can waste a lot of water in a year.
You can also reuse water. Water from washing vegetables can water your plants. Every drop counts. If everyone saves a little, together we can save a lot.

drop.def: a very small amount of liquid
drop.g: Every drop counts 每一滴都算數。

season.def: one of the parts of the year

tap.def: a thing that controls water from a pipe

shower.def: washing your body under running water
shower.ex: I take a shower every night.

leak.def: a hole where water comes out
leak.ex: There is a leak in the roof.

drip.g: a dripping tap 滴水的水龍頭。

grammar.pt: only a very small part of
grammar.ex: only a very small part of it is fresh water

articles.title: Birds That Cannot Fly
articles.note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly. Instead, they are excellent swimmers. Their wings work like flippers and help them move quickly through the water to catch fish.
Most penguins live in the southern half of the world. Some live in very cold places like Antarctica, but others live on warmer coasts in South America and Africa.
Penguins often live in large groups. Parents take turns keeping their eggs warm and finding food. Today, some kinds of penguins are in danger because the oceans are changing.

penguin.def: a black and white bird that swims

wing.def: the part a bird uses to fly

coast.g: warmer coasts 較溫暖的海岸。

turn.def: the time for one person to do something

danger.g: be in danger 面臨危險。

grammar.ex: Some live in very cold places like Antarctica, but others live on warmer coasts
Parents take turns keeping their eggs warm

questions.q: What are penguins very good at?

opts: In the southern half of the world

keySentences.s: Penguins often live in large groups.

articles.title: The Story of Paper
articles.note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 A2-B1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Paper is so common that we rarely think about it. But for most of history, people wrote on stone, wood, cloth or animal skins.

Paper making was developed in ancient China about two thousand years ago. People mixed plant fibers with water, spread the mix thin and let it dry. Later, the idea slowly spread to other parts of the world.
Today, paper is made mostly from wood. Recycling paper saves trees, water and energy. Next time you finish with a newspaper or a box, put it in the recycling bin.

common.g: so common that… 如此常見以至於…。

rarely.g: 頻率副詞，本身就是否定意味。

history.g: for most of history 在歷史上大部分時間。

spread.def: to open out over a surface; to move to more places

grammar.ex: Paper is so common that we rarely think about it.
Paper making was developed in ancient China
spread the mix thin and let it dry

questions.q: What did people write on before paper?

keySentences.s: Today, paper is made mostly from wood.

articles.title: The secret to a happy life: lessons from 8 decades of research
articles.zh: 幸福人生的秘密：八十年研究的啟示

source.name: TED：Robert Waldinger, The secret to a happy life: lessons from 8 decades of research

articles.note: 內容主題取自 TED 熱門演講。內文為學習用改寫，不是講者原話，請看原演講了解細節。
paras: Robert Waldinger leads a famous study that has followed people's lives for more than eight decades. In this later talk, he shares more of what the study has taught him.
The main message is simple but powerful: our relationships matter a lot for a happy and healthy life. Good relationships are like muscles. If we do not use them, they get weaker.
He suggests small actions to keep relationships strong, like sending a message to an old friend or having a real conversation with someone at work. Who could you contact this week?

lead.g: leads 第三人稱單數；leader 名詞。

follow.def: to watch or go after something over time

matter.g: matter a lot 非常重要。

contact.def: to call or write to someone

If we do not use them, they get weaker.
like sending a message to an old friend
